module_title: Constitutional Bodies: EC, UPSC, and CAG - Basic Understanding
introduction: Constitutional bodies are those organizations that are mentioned directly in the Constitution of India. They derive their power and authority from the Constitution itself, making them highly independent and powerful.

core_concepts.title: Election Commission of India (Article 324)
core_concepts.description: The Election Commission is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India. It handles elections for the Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha), State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President.

core_concepts.title: Union Public Service Commission - UPSC (Article 315-323)
core_concepts.description: UPSC is the central recruiting agency in India. It conducts examinations for appointments to All-India Services (IAS, IPS, IFS) and Central Services (Group A & Group B).

core_concepts.title: Comptroller and Auditor General - CAG (Article 148)
core_concepts.description: The CAG is the 'Guardian of the Public Purse'. Its primary job is to audit the accounts of the Union and the States to ensure that public money is spent legally and efficiently.

core_concepts.title: Appointment and Tenure
core_concepts.description: The President of India appoints the members of these bodies. The typical tenure for the EC members, UPSC members, and the CAG is 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

important_entities.name: The President of India
important_entities.significance: All these high-ranking officials are appointed by the President, ensuring their status as top-tier constitutional authorities.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common mistake: The Election Commission of India (ECI) does NOT conduct elections for Panchayats and Municipalities. These are conducted by the 'State Election Commission'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember that EC, UPSC, and CAG all follow the same retirement/tenure rule: 6 years of service or 65 years of age.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the Article numbers: 324 (EC), 315 (UPSC), and 148 (CAG). These are frequently asked in direct match-the-following questions.
